doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Family and making music for the right reasons
summary: Allen says his grandchildren now like his work and that music is not about money but a product made from the heart.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I would say so. May I ask what your grandchildren think of your profession?
Well what a bunch of kids think, why are you doing it. And now they see that I’m doing it and they like it.

When I was doing it I wasn’t making much money and stuff so everybody was — oh why don’t you do this to make some money. It wasn’t about money, it was about preparing the goods and then you sell it. Then you will spend your time making a product of work, then it will sell itself. You see what I mean? But if you’re worrying about material money and all of this, and you put out a bad product it don’t last. What we put out is from the heart and from hard sweat, and no other values, not that, until we finished a product and you put it out there and it goes. It sells itself.
And then you’re on to the next one.
